schema_intro: Derived by `audit/b3/levels_walk.py` from the four sensor drivers' declared schemas, read by `tests/_schema_cases.py`'s `declared_fields()` and `domain_cases()` (every `_VAL_*` schema and module-level FieldSchema: each bound from below, at it and from above, a set's edges and first gap, both bools and a non-bool, None, and NaN/+inf/-inf for a float field), then each `# @limits` tag of their constructors. A schema row maps to its driver's L1 sweep, which drives every case through the PUT path (`_set_dict_cfg()`, ContMeas/ResetVOC/Calibrate included) or, for SGP40's compensation inputs, the read path, and names every case that answered against its declared domain. A row bites when that sweep is verdicted biting and a plant of the row's own check class (`levels_data.json` `schema_plants`: one check broken in a private copy first on MICROPYPATH) made it report that row at gc -1 and at 32768, zero memory markers (agent, 2026-10-28). The rows of the `# @limits` tags are L0's, where buildgen's validation is the claim. Combinations of fields are CM3's (the config-value dimensions), not this section's.

dash_reasons.reason: the package's docstring alone: no behaviour to test
host build tooling (CPython) that runs before any MicroPython level: those levels test its output, the generated modules' rows; L0 is its level (E.6.1)
build-time overrides of the Unix port: every L1/L2 file runs on the binary they shaped, none names them; L0 checks each override's anchor
the host toolchain builder: L0 tests it and L3 boots the firmware it builds; no MicroPython level runs it
host scripts: L0 is their level (E.6.1); the runners among them are how L1-L4 execute, not code those levels test
website JavaScript: L0 (vitest) is its level; L2's real-website scenarios serve the built bundle on every device without naming each file
CI configuration: GitHub Actions runs it and L0 checks it statically; no MicroPython or board level executes it
runs a device script on the twin for tests_hardware's twin mode; L0 tests it (test_twin_board.py)
the twin is L2's stand-in for the hardware; L3 and L4 run the real board in its place
MicroPython twin code: L0 reads a twin file only where a static check needs it; the L2 files that run it are its level
twin code: L2 is its level; L1 runs on tests/'s own fakes
pure MicroPython codec logic with no tag, schema or constant a host check reads
pure computation, the same on silicon: L1 proves it and L2 runs it in the booted graph; silicon adds no path of its own
no network-facing behaviour: L4 is L3 plus the WiFi bridge, and this module's silicon behaviour is its L3 cell's
network-facing: L3 has no radio peer (no bridge), so its silicon behaviour is its L4 cell's
the no-autostart entry starts nothing: L1 proves it; the twin boots the autostart graph

the flash and bench tiers flash the autostart image; the no-autostart image (build_firmware.py --no-autostart) only starts nothing, proven at L1 and at L0, and a silicon check would cost an extra flash cycle

functional_intro: Derived by the walk, one row per `src/` module: its real consumers in the generated graph (the `src/` modules a generated device reaches that import it, and the generated module where that imports it directly), and the L2 functions that drive it in a generated device's graph: a function of its matrix row's L2 cell that is also in the generated module's L2 cell, else the same for its first consumer that has one (named "through"). The devices are those the biting ones run on: a twin CI scenario on every device wiring its drivers, a construction scenario or a `PER_DEVICE` file on every device, any other twin test on the device its file picks (SPECIFICATION.md E.2.1). A row bites when such a function is verdicted biting and the module is booted (agent, 2026-10-28).
system_intro: First one row per REST route of the generated API reference (`build/generated_src/api/<device>.json`), derived: the L2 functions whose code, or a helper of their file, names the route's method and path, and the devices they run on (as above). Then one row per top-level feature of SPECIFICATION.md A.2 and per item of A.4's "functional behaviors confirmed intentional" list, with its tests named by hand (`levels_data.json` `system_rows`); a module-internal item names the lowest level that proves it. Recovery paths are `conformance.md`'s rows (A.U35.52's rungs), cited there, not repeated here (agent, 2026-10-28).
ladder_intro: The multi-chunk SET at each level, named by hand and joined with review.md's verdict. A.U26.87's re-home touches no `src/` file: its commit `0c0ad52c` (the U26 close, the commit that added `uart_link_echo_under_serving_load.py`) has an empty `git diff --stat 0c0ad52c^1 0c0ad52c -- src`. The second L2 test already carries a 140-byte, three-chunk SET while the graph's noise tasks run (`tests/test_digital_twin_uart_link.py:750-770`), so it owes no extension; UM4's merge is not in this base either way (agent, 2026-10-28).
narrowings_intro: Each test that deliberately runs on one device, the device it takes, and the row whose tests cover the other devices (agent, 2026-10-28).
